# Protected-metric follow-up for PRs #3117, #3086 and #3109

This task-scoped workflow lives on `perf/ubuntu-aba-metrics-20260907`. Product code and the scheduled workflows on main are unchanged. Exact main and candidate SHAs are workflow inputs. Candidates must contain pinned main. Each job runs on one GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` VM; each measurement suite uses A1, B, A2. Both binaries and fixtures are built before measurement. Raw reports identify the actual image, CPU, runtime, harness commit, and DLL hashes. A workflow success means evidence collection completed, not acceptance.

## Questions and workloads

- **#3117:** Do dispatch timing/allocation gains hold for CPU and queue latency, including pending paired handlers? Four existing lifetime benchmarks collect process CPU and enqueue-to-handler-entry latency as additional diagnostics. Their raw latency samples cover the last lifetime only, while CPU spans all measured lifetimes; these are not end-to-end completion metrics. Separate real Kafka workloads exercise public key-ordered record and batch processing, with two handlers per partition, 128 buffered records, and batches up to 16. The loaded handlers complete synchronously. Review both suites together; loaded synchronous handlers do not establish arbitrary asynchronous-handler performance.
- **#3086:** Does the successful fetch path regress with realistic records? Real Kafka workloads consume sequentially with prefetch depths 1 and 3. Existing focused BDN cases separately isolate successful foreground/prefetch handling, follower errors, leader errors, and response pooling. Empty-response error rows measure fetch operations, not messages. Candidate follower-recovery unit/integration tests assert offsets and delivery; the baseline's known incorrect reset is explicitly asserted by the fixture adapter. No fabricated performance comparison for the different recovery behavior.
- **#3109:** Does a full-queue shutdown remain efficient, correct, and bounded? BDN measures stop-only timing/allocations. An additional probe repeats 10,000 complete 1,024-record queue lifetimes and records every stop latency. Process CPU, allocations, and throughput cover the whole lifecycle, including setup and verification; they are not stop-only costs. Each repetition verifies the final checkpoint, all processed records, queue drain, and rejection of blocked writers. Candidate backpressure/runtime unit tests cover in-flight commits, cancellation, stalled lanes, and shared deadlines. Kafka integration tests verify broker commits during backpressure and drain. Per-message steady-state latency is not applicable to this shutdown-only probe; operation latency is reported instead.

## Loaded consumer measurement

Use Kafka `apache/kafka:4.3.1`, four partitions, 256-byte values, 1,024 integer keys, and a fixed offered rate of 50,000 messages/second. Offer groups of 100 on a monotonic schedule. Do not shift the schedule when the producer falls behind. Warm up for 20 seconds, then offer measured traffic for 120 seconds per mode. Drain every offered message with a fixed watchdog. Both modes run in every phase; each phase starts a fresh broker and uses fresh topics/processes. Dry validation uses 1,000 messages/second for 2 measured seconds on separate brokers.

Pin broker to CPU 0, a separate baseline-built producer to CPU 1, and consumer to CPUs 2/3. Reject runners without those CPUs. The producer binary is identical across A1/B/A2. Capture producer acknowledgements, failures and maximum scheduling debt, plus broker CPU/memory statistics. A saturated producer/broker or persistent scheduling debt limits the conclusions; constant offered throughput alone cannot establish maximum consumer capacity.

Use the same SDK/runtime and default tiered compilation for all loaded phases. BDN retains its fixed tiered-compilation-off configuration. Latency is scheduled producer offer to synchronous handler observation/completion (immediately before returning), including producer pacing debt, broker time, and consumer queueing. It excludes automatic completion tracking after the handler returns. Store every measured latency before computing p50/p99/max. Validate sequence uniqueness, per-key order, partition routing, and exact delivered/acknowledged counts. No sampled-message extrapolation or discarded tail outliers.

CPU is client process CPU time divided by completed measured messages. Whole-process allocated bytes include amortized fetch/dispatch and low-frequency harness sampling. The CPU/allocation window starts at the first measured completion and ends at the last completion; report its actual duration. BDN and the warmed dispatch allocation probe provide isolated allocation attribution. Collect one-second completed counts, scheduled offered counts/backlog, cumulative CPU, allocated bytes, GC counts, managed heap and RSS. Preallocate latency arrays before startup. These two-minute windows test short sustained stability, not multi-hour leak absence.

## Decision rules declared before dispatch

Protect throughput, CPU, allocations, p50/p99/max latency, correctness and stability together. No approved performance tradeoffs exist for these runs. Retain any confirmed loss even if another metric improves; do not silently add a percentage allowance. The #3086 experiment must resolve the previously observed 3–5% successful-prefetch question before claiming equivalence.

Report absolute A1/B/A2 values and deltas against each control separately. Assess uncertainty and control drift using raw BDN distributions and loaded time series; adjacent per-message samples are correlated and cannot be treated as independent replications. Check tail windows, maxima, backlog drain, failures, memory/GC trends, producer pacing and broker saturation. Missing metrics, insufficient precision, materially drifting controls, or a workload bottleneck yield `INCONCLUSIVE`. A confirmed protected-metric loss yields `REGRESSION`; complete evidence satisfying all applicable requirements permits `PASS`. Broad correctness/stability conclusions require the targeted tests as well as timing results. No automatic gate promotion is implemented.

Retain failed Dry runs and invalid experiments. The existing one-repeat limit applies to an inconclusive exact experiment. These are new causal workload measurements, not identical repetitions of the earlier timing-only suite. Review all same-SHA evidence and prior concerns before funding another repeat or changing the exact-head gate.
